_comment: The codex: what the world is and how it works, in the world's own words. Creature pages live with the creatures (world_objects/config/world_objects.json) and rune pages with the runes (runes.json); this file holds the rest. An entry may wait on a flag, so a page never describes a mechanic the server is not running. At most three sentences a page, except the first.

entries.title: The Old Roads
entries._note: Signed by its byline; she was asked to keep it short.
body: Every road was written once. The people who made them cut a rune where two ways met, and the rune said what the road was for: this one to water, this one to market, this one home. The land read the runes and kept to them. That was the arrangement.
The people were waywrights, and there were four trades of them. They are covered elsewhere and would want it noted that they got on.

People still use the roads. Nobody reads them. Signposts do the work, and a signpost says where a road goes without saying what it is for. A road that is used and not read goes vague. That is the fog. It is not weather and it is not dangerous. It is ground that has stopped being sure of itself.
Things settle in the vague parts. They are small and local and have habits. None of them is in charge.
The cure is not complicated. Go out and read. What you have read goes in the book, and the book does not forget; that is what it is for.

entries.title: The fog
body: Ground you have not read. Plenty of people have passed it. That is not the same thing.

entries.title: Read ground
body: What you have read goes in the book, and stays there. The fog does not come back over it. The book does not forget; that is what it is for.

entries.title: Runes
body: A mark cut where two ways met, saying what the road was for. A stave cannot be ridden, so each rune has a road form: what it comes out as when the knife is a road. Rune-stones work loose; frost, roadworks, a council with a budget.

entries.title: Things that settle
body: Things settle where nobody is paying attention. A busy road will do. They are not evil; they are in the way.

entries.title: Hold
body: How firmly a thing has settled. Effort near it loosens it, and so does what you did on the way. Enough, and it is seen off.

entries.title: What a thing wants
body: Each thing wants something done about it: the road used, new ground, height, a rune cut round it, or the word written down. Each shrugs at something else. The card says which.

entries.title: Moving on
body: Three days and a thing finds somewhere quieter. It is not seen off; it is elsewhere.

entries.title: Boxes
body: A chisel, some chalk and the day's tolls, buried when the gate closed. The waywrights left them on the understanding that somebody would come back. You are somebody.

entries.title: Old coin
body: The roads pay in old coin. Nobody will change it for you. It buys what the roads sell, and nothing else.

entries.title: The book
body: Every coin in and every coin out. Nothing is yours until it is in the book. Then it is yours, and I have a copy.

entries.title: The reckoning
body: The count at the end of an outing: what was read, what was found, what was paid. It is done once, carefully, and reopened from the journal whenever you like.

entries.title: The board
body: Notices. Somewhere to go, and why. Taken down when done, or after a fortnight.

entries.title: Today's bounty
body: One thing a day, not there the day before. Double, because it is on a road people use.

entries.title: Levels
body: How well the roads know you. It goes up slowly and never down.

entries.title: Titles
body: What the board calls you. Earned, never bought.

entries.title: Days kept
body: A road walked daily stays open. A kilometre a day keeps it.

entries.title: Sixes
body: One rune is a word. Six is a sentence, and the land can read a sentence. A full six pays, once.

entries.title: The four trades
body: Wayfinders went ahead, Cutters kept the runes legible, Menders carried the stone and Clerks wrote it all down. Your trade shapes your notices and what pays best. It never locks you out of anything.

entries.title: Knacks
body: Something your trade teaches you once it trusts you with it. A knack is chosen, kept, and kept to its own trade.

entries.title: A change of trade
body: The first is free. After that, one hundred and fifty, and a day's wait. The old trade keeps your place.

entries.title: A lamp left out
body: Leave a lamp at a place and something comes to see who is passing. Fifty coins, for the oil.

entries.title: Places found
body: Named places hold their own. They are the last thing the fog takes, and the first thing a reader finds.

entries.title: The Wayfinders
body: They went ahead and decided where the road would go. Agnes Fell walked off the county map and sent back a corrected one. Their saying: the edge moves.

entries.title: The Cutters
body: They kept the runes legible, which mostly meant cutting them again. Tobias Marrow could read a milestone by hand in the dark and was wrong about most other things. Their saying: look twice, then once more.

entries.title: The Menders
body: They carried the stone. Hester Cragg carried the same stone up the same hill until it stayed. Their saying: the hill does not negotiate.

entries.title: The Clerks
body: They kept the toll-book and everything else. Edmund Pell wrote down the weather for forty years and is the only reason anybody knows it rained. Their saying: it may as well be you.
